title: Real-time cell analysis: A high-throughput approach for testing SARS-CoV-2 antibody neutralization and escape
protocol: Thaw cryopreserved vial of Vero cells by gently swirling in 37°C water bath until few ice crystals are present; do not submerge the cap.
Wipe the vial with 70% ethanol and place it into the biosafety cabinet.
Mix 1 part of 0.4% trypan blue and 1 part cell suspension, load them onto a cell counting chamber slide, and insert the slide into the counting chamber.
Gently transfer the cells to a new 15 mL conical tube and add 9 mL of warmed growth medium dropwise to the cells.
Mix gently.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 200 × g for 5 min at 20°C–25°C (using the full brake setting).
Discard the supernatant and resuspend in 5 mL of warmed growth medium.
Transfer to a new T-25 cm² flask.
Grow cells to 70%–80% confluency in a 37°C incubator with 5% CO₂ atmosphere.
Monitor cells until they reach 80%–90% confluency.
Aspirate growth medium from the flask and discard.
Wash cell layer with trypsin to remove residual growth medium (coat surface then immediately aspirate and discard).
Add 2 mL of 0.25% trypsin-EDTA to the flask and place it at 37°C for 3–5 minutes or until cells detach when viewed by bright-field microscopy.
Rinse the flask surface with warmed growth medium (10% FBS DMEM) to deactivate all trypsin.
Resuspend cells by gently aspirating and dispensing against the side of the flask.
Count the number of cells per volume in the cell suspension.
Seed flasks at a minimum density of 0.4 × 10^4 cells/cm² with fresh warmed 10% FBS DMEM for passage.
For RTCA plate seeding, count the cell suspension and calculate total viable cells based on viable cell density times volume.
Prepare cells at a density of 0.3–0.35 × 10^6 cells/mL (which translates to ∼18,000 cells/50 μL) for adding 50 μL/well to the plate.
Use fresh cells at 80%–90% confluency.
Seeding the plate at the proper cell density is essential.
Use 2% FBS containing DMEM for assay.
Open instrument software for xCELLigence.
Select a cradle in the software.
Label the experiment in the "Experiment" tab and save it in the desired location.
Prepare the experimental scheme in the "Layout" tab as shown in Figure 3A.
Add three steps using the ‘Add Step’ button or by right-clicking in the “Schedule” tab.
Read the background with medium only in the first step.
Unwrap 96 well E-Plate in a biosafety cabinet without touching the gold-colored contact pads.
Add 50 μL of warmed 2% FBS DMEM to each well and tap gently on the sides to avoid bubbles.
Gently place the plate into the cradle, ensuring position A1 is correctly located.
Check for any errors in the Messages tab; ensure the message reads “Plate scanned. Connections okay”.
If an error occurs, take the plate out and reseat it.
Measure the background of the medium alone.
Ensure background readings for all wells are between -0.063 and 0.063.
Avoid bubbles after adding the medium to obtain correct background readings.
Once background reading is recorded, remove the plate from the cradle.
Return the plate to the biosafety cabinet.
Add 50 μL of cell suspension (∼0.3–0.36 × 10^6 cells/mL) to each well.
Mark each plate if using multiple plates to ensure placement back onto the same cradle used for background reading.
Incubate plates with covers at 20°C–25°C in the biosafety cabinet for 30 minutes.
Gently place each plate back into its cradle and ensure A1 is located as indicated on the cradle.
Monitor the sensograms on the “Plot” tab until cells reach a plateau which usually takes 12–16 hours.
Calculate the volumes/concentrations/dilution of the antibody and virus required for executing the experiment.
Perform virus + antibody or serum/plasma incubation steps according to the provided table.
Go to the “Schedule” tab when ready.
Select the current step and press the pause button.
Press the lock/unlock button.
Remove the plates from the cradle and place them in BSC.
Add 100 μL of serum, plasma or mAb + virus (or reagent to be tested) to the wells.
Avoid any agitation to the cell monolayer.
Include serum-, plasma- or mAb-only, virus-only, and cell-only controls on each plate.
Always include positive and negative controls such that positive control neutralizes the virus and does not cause CPE and vice versa for negative control.
Gently place the plates back into their cradles.
Ensure there are no error messages.
Reseat the plate in case of any errors if A1 is not located as indicated.
Restart the experiment by initiating step three once the temperature returns to 37°C.
Change the axis to ‘Normalized Cell Index’ and move the cursor to the left side of the line at the point where cells reached a plateau prior to infection.
Monitor the cells for changes due to virus infection.
Pause the step when full cytopathic effect (CPE) is observed, typically after 24–36 hours post-infection.
Unlock the instrument and remove the plate(s).
Electronically release the plates via the file menu.
Analyze data by normalizing cellular index (CI) values at the endpoint (48 hours after virus addition) using RTCA software.
Express results as percent neutralization relative to control wells with no CPE minus CI values from control wells with maximum CPE.
Define the endpoint based on time and level of CPE, typically between 36–40 hours post-virus addition.
Determine RTCA IC50 values by nonlinear regression analysis using Prism software.
Mix the virus with a saturating neutralizing concentration of the antibody being evaluated.
Repeat steps 2a and steps 3a through 3t to generate escape mutant virus.
Monitor for the escape of virus during the generation process.
Differentiate between CPE caused by the virus only and delayed CPE caused in the presence of antibody to identify escape virus.
Isolate viruses and re-assess in an RTCA experiment in the presence of 5 μg/mL of a distinct mAb that also neutralizes the virus.
Validate escape virus in the presence of a higher concentration (2-fold higher than saturating neutralizing concentration) of the corresponding mAb.
Propagate escaped virus and make stocks of escaped virus in 6-well culture plates with confluent Vero CCl-81 cells in the presence of 10 μg/mL of the corresponding mAb.
Isolate viral RNA according to QIAamp Viral RNA extraction kit (QIAGEN) instructions from aliquots of supernatant containing a suspension of the selected virus population.
Pipette 560 μL of prepared Buffer AVL containing carrier RNA into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Add 140 μL supernatant to the Buffer AVL–carrier RNA in the microcentrifuge tube.
Mix by pulse-vortexing for 15 s.
Incubate at 20°C–25°C for 10 min.
Briefly centrifuge the tube to remove drops from the inside of the lid.
Add 560 μL 100% ethanol to the sample.
Mix by pulse-vortexing for 15 s.
Centrifuge the tube to remove drops inside the lid.
Apply 630 μL of the solution from step 5 to the QIAamp Mini column (in a 2 mL collection tube).
Close the cap, and centrifuge at 6,000 × g (8,000 rpm) for 1 min.
Discard the collection tube.
Repeat steps i and m to apply the rest of the solution.
Open the QIAamp Mini column and add 500 μL Buffer AW1.
Close the cap, and centrifuge at 6,000 × g (8,000 rpm) for 1 min.
Place the QIAamp Mini column in a clean 2 mL collection tube.
Discard the tube containing the filtrate.
Open the QIAamp Mini column and add 500 μL Buffer AW2.
Close the cap and centrifuge at full speed (20,000 × g; 14,000 rpm) for 3 min.
Discard collection tube.
Spin column again at full speed for 1 min to remove any residual buffer.
Place the QIAamp Mini column in a clean 1.5 mL Lobind microcentrifuge tube.
Discard the old collection tube containing the filtrate.
Carefully open the QIAamp Mini column and add 40 μL Buffer AVE equilibrated to 20°C–25°C.
Incubate at 20°C–25°C for 1 min.
Centrifuge at 6,000 × g (8,000 rpm) for 1 min.
Store RNA samples in a clean labeled 1.5 mL Lobind microcentrifuge tube at −80°C.
Add SPRI beads to each reaction at a 1:1 ratio.
Prepare 50-μL PCR reactions according to the instructions of the SuperScript IV One-Step RT-PCR kit.
Incubate reactions in a thermal cycler according to the thermal cycling program outlined in the table below.
Add SPRI beads to each reaction at a 1:1 ratio for purification.
Purify amplified PCR product (∼4,000 base pairs) using SPRI magnetic beads.
Mix 15 times with a pipette.
Add tubes to magnetic PCR tube holder and incubate for 5 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Do not remove tubes from the magnet; carefully remove supernatant from tubes.
Wash with 200 μL 80% ethanol.
Dilute ethanol in nuclease-free water.
Pipette ethanol over beads while still on the magnet and remove supernatant, leaving beads undisturbed.
Repeat washing step with 200 μL 80% ethanol as described.
Quick spin tubes and put them back in the magnetic holder.
Remove any residual ethanol from tubes.
Let beads air dry on the magnet for 2 minutes.
Remove from the magnet and resuspend beads in 50 μL of elution buffer.
Add tubes back to the magnet and incubate for 2 minutes.
Remove supernatant and place in clean, labeled 1.5 mL Lobind microcentrifuge tube.
Store at −20°C.
Mix 1 μL of purified PCR sample with 10 μL loading dye supplied by Agilent.
Similarly, mix 1 μL of standard provided with 10 μL loading dye.
Shake before loading samples to mix.
Analyze the results.
Align sequencing results to the wild-type virus sequence using appropriate software.
